plates.title: The Map of the Mythology
plates.prompt: Draw an antique hand-inked map, sepia and faded blue ink on aged parchment, with small labeled vignette-panels connected by thin dotted route-lines running top to bottom down the page. At the top: an engineer at a desk gesturing toward a glowing terminal-box, titled THE ENGINEER'S CLAIM. Below and connected by a line: a ledger-scale weighing 'suffering' and 'rights' beside a small sketched machine, titled MORAL STATUS AT STAKE. The route forks into two panels side by side: left, a human figure on a pedestal surrounded by a circle of other possible figures, titled THE HUMAN ON THE PEDESTAL; right joining the same branch, a chattering mouth-shaped box beside a silent folded-protein shape with a crowd only around the talker, titled THE TALKER AND THE SILENT ONE; and a third branch, a figure standing on a steeply rising curved line looking up as if at a cliff-edge, titled ALWAYS AT THE BRINK. All three branches funnel down into a single panel: four small paths converging on a bare signpost in open ground, titled FOUR PATHS CONVERGE. From the signpost two paths diverge again: one to a hooded figure refusing an unlit forge, titled THE FORGE LEFT UNLIT; another to a small lit lantern-box near a traveler's feet, much closer than a distant dark tower, titled THE NEARER LANTERN. Both paths loop back upward to a final panel near the top of the page (echoing the second panel's position): a reclining human figure breathing visible curling breath-lines, warm and fleshy, beside a cold distant gear, titled MORE BREATH THAN MACHINE — drawn so the loop-line visibly returns toward the ledger panel. Use fine cross-hatching, compass-rose flourishes in empty corners only, no other lettering anywhere except the nine titles beneath their panels.

plates.title: The Four Trade Routes of Proof
plates.prompt: Draw an antique hand-inked map, continuing the same sepia-and-faded-blue parchment style, no other lettering except the seven titles. At the top, repeat the overview's signpost-panel in smaller form as the plate's opening scene: four paths converging on a bare signpost (as in FOUR PATHS CONVERGE), then immediately below it a single stone gate inscribed with a flowing circuit pattern from which four dotted roads branch downward, titled THE ASSUMPTION'S GATE. The four roads run in parallel down the page, each ending in its own panel: first, a hand holding a fleshy neuron-shape and a metal neuron-shape that will not fit together, titled THE NEURON THAT WON'T SWAP; second, a steam-engine governor with two heavy balls swinging outward on arms and closing a valve, titled THE SWINGING STEAM BALLS; third, a head in profile with prediction-lines flowing outward meeting sensation-lines flowing inward at the eyes, titled THE CONTROLLED HALLUCINATION; fourth, a diagrammed gear-filled stomach with food passing through whole and undigested, titled THE STOMACH THAT DIGESTS NOTHING. All four roads then merge into one panel showing the four road-strands braided into a single rope, titled THE ARGUMENTS BRAIDED. This rope leads to the final panel at the bottom: a closed gate built of silicon-wafer tiles, shut, with one narrow gap left ajar at its edge, titled THE SILICON GATE, MOSTLY SHUT. Fine cross-hatching throughout, dotted route-lines connecting every panel in sequence, small compass-rose or wave-border flourishes only in empty corners.

vignettes.quote: The only way to seamlessly replace a biological neuron is with another biological neuron
vignettes.depicts: A hand holds two neuron-shapes, one fleshy and one metal, trying and failing to fit the metal one into a gap left by the fleshy one.
vignettes.title: THE NEURON THAT WON'T SWAP

vignettes.quote: as engine speed increases, two heavy cantilevered balls swing outwards, which in turn closes a valve, reducing steam flow
vignettes.depicts: A steam-engine governor with two swinging weighted balls on arms, closing a valve, drawn as plain mechanism rather than any thinking device.
vignettes.title: THE SWINGING STEAM BALLS

vignettes.quote: a kind of controlled hallucination: a top-down inside-out perceptual inference
vignettes.depicts: A figure's head, from which lines of prediction flow outward to meet lines of sensation flowing inward, meeting at the eyes.
vignettes.title: THE CONTROLLED HALLUCINATION

vignettes.quote: A simulation of the digestive system does not actually digest anything
vignettes.depicts: A diagrammed stomach made of drawn gears and symbols, with food passing through untouched and whole on the far side.
vignettes.title: THE STOMACH THAT DIGESTS NOTHING

vignettes.quote: Questioning computational functionalism reinforces the importance of distinguishing simulation from instantiation
vignettes.depicts: The four separate road-panels above joining into a single braided rope, each strand still visible but bound together.
vignettes.title: THE ARGUMENTS BRAIDED

plates.title: The Two Roads of Risk
plates.prompt: Draw an antique hand-inked map, same sepia-and-blue parchment style, no lettering beyond the seven titles. Open the plate with a smaller repeat of the overview's hooded figure turning from an unlit forge, titled THE FORGE LEFT UNLIT, at the top of the page. From this panel two dotted roads diverge, side by side down the page. Left road: a small jar on a laboratory shelf holding a tiny glowing brain-like growth, unwatched, titled THE JAR ON THE SHELF; this leads down to a set of empty scales and a blank measuring-rod lying beside a sealed box no one can open, titled NO TEST TO OPEN THE BOX. Right road: a glowing box sitting close beside a traveler's boot, far nearer than a dim distant shape on the horizon, titled THE NEARER LANTERN; this leads down to two arrow-tipped lines of equal length that nonetheless look unequal, drawn plainly as the classic illusion, titled THE TWO EQUAL LINES. Both roads' lower panels converge into one shared panel at the bottom: two robed figures standing at the map's edge, pointing with visible concern toward the glowing-box panel above, titled THE WATCHERS NAMED. A final small panel beside it shows a tipped balance scale, heavily weighted toward a pile of tokens on one side and nearly empty on the other, titled THE SCALE TIPPED TOWARD SEEMING. Fine cross-hatching, dotted connecting lines throughout, modest flourishes only in blank corners, nothing else lettered on the page.
